Name: Asami Kojiro
Information:
**Asami Kojiro**

A human child born to a noble who moved to Cu Chullis during the reign of the Somonian Empire. Their father, a moon elf related to a vassal family of the Elmanda clan, fell in love with a human woman, who gave birth to Asami Kojirō. Due to being a human with the blood of elven nobility, it became necessary to hide her and train her to defend herself, which revealed in her teenage years that she was an excellent warrior by nature.

Asami trained primarily in defensive techniques, learning to counter attacks, keep others at a distance, and wield a weapon that made up for her perceived frailty as a woman (an accusation she found overly traditional and rallied against). In adulthood, she formed a romantic relationship with a prolific elven swordsmith who forged a weapon for her that they claimed would “capture Asami’s beauty and strength”- the washing pole. Though unfamiliar with its strange construction at first, and lacking the smith to guide her after they returned to Cu Chullis, Asami eventually came to realize that with proper tempering it could be wielded one-handed, despite its huge size.

**Wandering Blade**

In her late twenties, Asami left her family in search of personal fulfillment. She was a half-elven human woman raised by a traditional Cu Chullian family, and so turned heads in Retia quickly. While travelling, she became famous for her skill as a one-woman army who could handle any threat that tried to take advantage of her, which would eventually cause certain thrill-seekers to hunt her down, proclaim themselves her rivals, and try to kill “the White Blade of Cu Chullis,” a nickname she picked up. She dispatched all challengers, and while searching Retia for sites of natural beauty to meditate and educate herself, staving off aggressors became a regular part of life. This practical combat experience only sharpened her skills further, and after several years she realized she could travel more easily and make connections working as a mercenary.

**An Equal Opponent**

Among her many rivals came an elven swordsman named Meirlach Musashi, who had fled from Cu Chullis after his grim reputation of abandoning his lords led to him no longer finding work among the nobles he enjoyed exploiting. This swordsman was as much a prodigy as Asami, and the two would encounter each other on happenstance several times. Sometimes they battled under different circumstances, and sometimes would fight beside each other. Both learned from watching the other, developing their skills using the other as the template for the perfect opponent.

People began to talk of the two as entangled - lovers to rivals or the other way around, depicted as hunting each other in an eternal game of cat and mouse. Musashi indulged in these rumors to drum up interest in himself, but Asami rejected them and grew to resent the attention her life had drawn to her.

**A Fateful Duel**

Hoping to escape from her fate by scaring people away forever, Asami found herself challenging Musashi to a very public duel, where she planned to lose dramatically and dispel rumors of her skill. However, Musashi saw through her intention and had one of the few compassionate moments in his hedonistic life: he refused to let her disgrace herself. Instead, he telegraphed his intentions and blindsided her, pretending to blind her using the sun behind him, and struck a “fatal blow.” She seemed to die, defeated and embarrassed. Musashi fled with her body, not allowing anyone to confirm her death.

She recovered quickly, and the two encouraged rumors of her death. Musashi would go on to spread rumors about Asami (confusing legends of her gender, species, intentions, etc.) while Asami assumed a quiet identity and avoided notice.

**Death and Legacy**

Eventually, Asami would begin succumbing to old age even in spite of her elven blood. She sent for Musashi, who she considered a dear friend, who she wished to see at its end. He arrived, and she asked the two duel in earnest. The two fought for two days, until Asami allowed herself to be slain by Musashi. Knowing he had a tainted legacy, she wished for him to have this accomplishment and wished to have died by his hands. In this encounter, Musashi discovered a truth about the world that would define his own legacy, which no other swordsman has yet to reach.

Musashi erected a shrine to his fallen adversary, which would be tended to by a small number of his students in secret. Those wishing to learn the way of the White Blade of Cu Chullis would seek it out to pray there. Asami’s spirit, fulfilled but still waiting for a true defeat with no interfering circumstances, would become bound to the shrine and is said to appear to those who might fulfill her desire for a final, true defeat.

traits.name: Deflection Master
traits.description: Unless they are incapacitated, the spirit is resistant to piercing and slashing damage, and ranged attacks made against them have disadvantage.

traits.name: Intercept
traits.description: Attacks made against the spirit’s allies while they are within reach of its Spirit Uchigatana have disadvantage, unless the spirit is incapacitated.

traits.name: Sparrow Slayer
traits.description: When you have advantage on a weapon attack, it deals one additional die of damage on a hit.

traits.name: Unwavering Saint
traits.description: If the spirit is reduced to 0 hit points, the creature who defeated it must roll a d100. On a result equal to or less than twice the damage dealt to the saint that exceeded its hit points, it is successfully reduced to 0 hit points. Otherwise, it is reduced to 1 hit point instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The spirit makes three weapon attacks.

actions.name: Spirit Uchigatana
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (4d6 + 6) slashing damage. When this attack hits a given creature that is Large or smaller for the first time each turn, they must make a DC 19 Strength saving throw. On a failure, they are knocked prone.

actions.name: Killing Slide (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The spirit chooses two points it can see, each within 60 feet of them, and within 30 feet of one another, then draws a line between both. Each creature in any of those spaces (except the spirit) is assailed by a space-cutting strike, and must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw. Creatures occupying three or more of those spaces have disadvantage. Each creature that fails takes 83 (15d10) slashing damage, or half as much damage on a success.

bonus_actions.name: Fortify Stance
bonus_actions.description: If the spirit has taken no movement on its turn, it can take the Dodge action as part of this bonus action and gain a +2 bonus to melee weapon attacks until the start of its next turn. It loses this bonus if it takes any movement willingly.

reactions.name: Sparrow Reversal (Recharge 4-6)
reactions.description: In response to being hit by an attack, the spirit can roll a weapon attack using its Spirit Uchigatana. If the attack result is higher than the attack result that hit it, the attacker misses automatically, and the spirit may continue to make similar attacks to attempt to negate each attack made by the same target until the end of the turn, as though it used this reaction multiple times. If at any point this fails to negate an attack, this effect ends.

legendary_reactions.source_conversion_note: Converted from Legendary Resistance (3/Day) per standing formatting rule.
